# nanoflow CLI reference

nanoflow is made by [nanosite.ai](https://nanosite.ai).

Every command takes `--json` (result on stdout, progress on stderr), `--dry` (print, change nothing) and `--yes` (answer confirmations; required without a TTY). `nf` is a short alias of `nanoflow`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`nanoflow task start`](#nanoflow-task-start) | kick off a task: issue → board In progress → worktree on its own ports → session/terminal title → opening comment |
| [`nanoflow task pr`](#nanoflow-task-pr) | PR is open: title gets `· PR #n`, board → In review (nanoflow pr create does this for you) |
| [`nanoflow task done`](#nanoflow-task-done) | PR merged: title gets ✓, board → Done; reminds you to tear the worktree down |
| [`nanoflow ticket new`](#nanoflow-ticket-new) | create an issue (labels + board Status) without starting work on it |
| [`nanoflow board set`](#nanoflow-board-set) | set an issue's Status (adds it to the board if missing) |
| [`nanoflow board list`](#nanoflow-board-list) | board issues in a column (default: ready, i.e. up for pickup) |
| [`nanoflow title`](#nanoflow-title) | (re)apply the session + terminal title for the current task branch |
| [`nanoflow wt create`](#nanoflow-wt-create) | add a worktree + branch for <ticket>-<slug> on the next free port slot; copy and patch shared files; install |
| [`nanoflow wt list`](#nanoflow-wt-list) | worktrees with their slot, branch and ports |
| [`nanoflow wt remove`](#nanoflow-wt-remove) | stop the worktree's processes, delete it, prune (refuses uncommitted/unpushed work unless --force); prints the agent cleanup checklist |
| [`nanoflow wt clean`](#nanoflow-wt-clean) | remove every worktree whose PR is merged or closed (asks first; --yes to confirm non-interactively) |
| [`nanoflow env`](#nanoflow-env) | this checkout's slot: each service's port and URL, and the env `up` exports |
| [`nanoflow up`](#nanoflow-up) | start this checkout's services on its slot ports, wait until they answer, print the URLs |
| [`nanoflow status`](#nanoflow-status) | which of this slot's services answer, and the --bg stack if one runs |
| [`nanoflow logs`](#nanoflow-logs) | show (or --follow) a service's log from the `nf up --bg` stack |
| [`nanoflow kill`](#nanoflow-kill) | stop this checkout's dev processes (the --bg stack + anything running from its dir), or a port's owner |
| [`nanoflow check`](#nanoflow-check) | run the repo's checks (checks in nanoflow.json); prints one line each, and only the tail of a failure |
| [`nanoflow pr create`](#nanoflow-pr-create) | push, open the PR (Conventional title + (#N), Closes #N), attach screenshots, board → In review, title |
| [`nanoflow pr comments`](#nanoflow-pr-comments) | unresolved review threads + conversation comments, condensed; reply in a thread or comment |
| [`nanoflow shots`](#nanoflow-shots) | upload screenshots to the screenshots branch (pr-<n>-<slug>/) and print or --attach the markdown |
| [`nanoflow ci`](#nanoflow-ci) | PR checks: status, --watch until done (no poll loops), the failing jobs' log tails, rerun failed |
| [`nanoflow flow`](#nanoflow-flow) | one snapshot of every worktree (slot, services up, ticket, PR, CI) and the open tickets; the nanoflow mod's provider |
| [`nanoflow summary`](#nanoflow-summary) | the wrap-up footer for the current task, from live state: worktree, branch, PR, ticket, done, local URL |
| [`nanoflow init`](#nanoflow-init) | write a starter .claude/nanoflow.json from what the repo has (scripts, lockfile, .env files); --team also offers the mod to teammates |
| [`nanoflow doctor`](#nanoflow-doctor) | check what nanoflow relies on: git, gh + auth, the config, the repo slug, the board |
| [`nanoflow docs`](#nanoflow-docs) | print (or --write docs/cli.md) the reference for every command |

### nanoflow task start

```text
Usage: nanoflow task start [options] [issue]

kick off a task: issue → board In progress → worktree on its own ports → session/terminal title →
opening comment

Arguments:
  issue                existing issue number to claim (or --new)

Options:
  --type <type>        issue type (ticket.types in nanoflow.json; default: the first one)
  --area <area>        area label, through ticket.labels.area
  --definition <text>  first body section (Definition, or Symptom for bugs)
  --plan <text>        second body section (Implementation plan, or Reproduction for bugs)
  --test-plan <text>   third body section
  --body <markdown>    full body, verbatim (skips the sections)
  --body-file <path>   full body from a file, verbatim
  --parent <issue>     link as a sub-issue of this epic
  --new <title>        create the issue first (takes the ticket options)
  --slug <slug>        worktree/branch slug (default: from the issue title)
  --title <short>      short session title, 2–4 words (default: from the issue title)
  --comment <text>     opening comment on the issue (default: names the branch)
  --no-install         skip the worktree's install step
  -h, --help           display help for command

Examples:
  nanoflow task start 651
  nf task start 651 --slug csv-export --title "csv export"
  nf task start --new "lease expires mid-post" --type bug
```

### nanoflow ticket new

```text
Usage: nanoflow ticket new [options] <title>

create an issue (labels + board Status) without starting work on it

Arguments:
  title                plain descriptive title

Options:
  --type <type>        issue type (ticket.types in nanoflow.json; default: the first one)
  --area <area>        area label, through ticket.labels.area
  --definition <text>  first body section (Definition, or Symptom for bugs)
  --plan <text>        second body section (Implementation plan, or Reproduction for bugs)
  --test-plan <text>   third body section
  --body <markdown>    full body, verbatim (skips the sections)
  --body-file <path>   full body from a file, verbatim
  --parent <issue>     link as a sub-issue of this epic
  --status <status>    board Status: backlog | ready | in-progress | in-review | done (default:
                       "ready")
  -h, --help           display help for command

Examples:
  nanoflow ticket new "csv export for orders" --definition "…"
  nf ticket new "checkout 500 on empty cart" --type bug --status backlog
  nf ticket new "phase 2" --parent 650 --body-file plan.md
```

### nanoflow board set

```text
Usage: nanoflow board set [options] <issue> <status>

set an issue's Status (adds it to the board if missing)

Arguments:
  issue       issue number, e.g. 651 or #651
  status      backlog | ready | in-progress | in-review | done

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  nf board set 651 in-progress
  nf board set 651 done --dry
```

### nanoflow board list

```text
Usage: nanoflow board list [options] [status]

board issues in a column (default: ready, i.e. up for pickup)

Arguments:
  status      backlog | ready | in-progress | in-review | done (default: "ready")

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  nf board list
  nf board list in-review --json
```

### nanoflow title

```text
Usage: nanoflow title [options]

(re)apply the session + terminal title for the current task branch

Options:
  --set <short>  store a new short title for this branch, then apply it
  --pr <n>       append `· PR #n`
  --merged       append ✓ (with --pr)
  -h, --help     display help for command

Examples:
  nf title
  nf title --set "lease expiry"
  nf title --pr 652 --merged
```

### nanoflow wt create

```text
Usage: nanoflow wt create [options] <name>

add a worktree + branch for <ticket>-<slug> on the next free port slot; copy and patch shared files;
install

Arguments:
  name          <ticket>-<slug>, e.g. 563-worktree-teardown

Options:
  --slot <n>    explicit slot (default: next free)
  --no-install  skip the install step
  -h, --help    display help for command

Examples:
  nf wt create 563-worktree-teardown
  nf wt create 563-x --slot 4 --no-install
```

### nanoflow wt list

```text
Usage: nanoflow wt list [options]

worktrees with their slot, branch and ports

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  nf wt list
  nf wt list --json
```

### nanoflow wt remove

```text
Usage: nanoflow wt remove [options] <name>

stop the worktree's processes, delete it, prune (refuses uncommitted/unpushed work unless --force);
prints the agent cleanup checklist

Arguments:
  name             worktree name, e.g. 563-worktree-teardown

Options:
  --delete-branch  also delete the local branch
  --force          discard uncommitted / unpushed work
  -h, --help       display help for command

Examples:
  nf wt remove 563-worktree-teardown --delete-branch
```

### nanoflow wt clean

```text
Usage: nanoflow wt clean [options]

remove every worktree whose PR is merged or closed (asks first; --yes to confirm non-interactively)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  nf wt clean --dry
  nf wt clean --yes
```

### nanoflow env

```text
Usage: nanoflow env [options]

this checkout's slot: each service's port and URL, and the env `up` exports

Options:
  --slot <n>   local slot (default: the current worktree's slot)
  --wt <name>  worktree whose slot to target
  -h, --help   display help for command

Examples:
  nf env
  nf env --wt 651-csv-export --json
  nf env --slot 0
```

### nanoflow up

```text
Usage: nanoflow up [options]

start this checkout's services on its slot ports, wait until they answer, print the URLs

Options:
  --with <names...>  also start these optional services
  --bg               run detached, logging to <stateDir>/logs/ (see nf logs / nf kill)
  --timeout <sec>    how long to wait for the services to answer
  --no-before        skip stack.before (e.g. building shared packages)
  -h, --help         display help for command

Examples:
  nf up --bg
  nf up --bg --with worker
  nf up            # foreground, Ctrl-C stops everything
```

### nanoflow status

```text
Usage: nanoflow status [options]

which of this slot's services answer, and the --bg stack if one runs

Options:
  --slot <n>   local slot (default: the current worktree's slot)
  --wt <name>  worktree whose slot to target
  -h, --help   display help for command

Examples:
  nf status
  nf status --slot 0 --json
```

### nanoflow logs

```text
Usage: nanoflow logs [options] <service>

show (or --follow) a service's log from the `nf up --bg` stack

Arguments:
  service        a service name from nanoflow.json

Options:
  --tail <n>     lines to show (default: "80")
  --grep <text>  only lines containing this (case-insensitive)
  --follow       keep printing new lines
  -h, --help     display help for command

Examples:
  nf logs server
  nf logs server --grep error --tail 200
  nf logs web --follow
```

### nanoflow kill

```text
Usage: nanoflow kill [options] [worktree]

stop this checkout's dev processes (the --bg stack + anything running from its dir), or a port's
owner

Arguments:
  worktree    another worktree's folder name (default: this checkout)

Options:
  --port <n>  stop whatever listens on this port instead
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  nf kill
  nf kill myapp-603-redirects
  nf kill --port 5173
```

### nanoflow check

```text
Usage: nanoflow check [options] [names...]

run the repo's checks (checks in nanoflow.json); prints one line each, and only the tail of a
failure

Arguments:
  names        which checks (default: all)

Options:
  --lines <n>  output lines shown per failing check (default: "40")
  -h, --help   display help for command

Examples:
  nf check
  nf check typecheck lint
  nf check test --json
```

### nanoflow pr create

```text
Usage: nanoflow pr create [options]

push, open the PR (Conventional title + (#N), Closes #N), attach screenshots, board → In review,
title

Options:
  --title <title>     PR title; ` (#N)` is appended if missing (default: the first feat/fix commit)
  --body <markdown>   PR body (Closes #N is appended if missing)
  --body-file <path>  PR body from a file
  --shots <files...>  screenshots to upload to the screenshots branch and embed
  --draft             open as a draft
  --no-push           don't push the branch first
  -h, --help          display help for command

Examples:
  nf pr create
  nf pr create --title "feat(web): add csv export" --body-file pr.md
  nf pr create --body-file pr.md --shots before.png after.png
```

### nanoflow pr comments

```text
Usage: nanoflow pr comments [options] [pr]

unresolved review threads + conversation comments, condensed; reply in a thread or comment

Arguments:
  pr                   PR number (default: the current branch's PR)

Options:
  --all                include resolved review threads
  --reply <commentId>  reply in the review thread of this comment id (with --body)
  --comment            post a top-level PR comment (with --body)
  --body <text>        text for --reply / --comment
  -h, --help           display help for command

Examples:
  nf pr comments
  nf pr comments 652 --all --json
  nf pr comments 652 --reply 2451234567 --body "fixed in 1a2b3c"
```

### nanoflow shots

```text
Usage: nanoflow shots [options] <pr> <files...>

upload screenshots to the screenshots branch (pr-<n>-<slug>/) and print or --attach the markdown

Arguments:
  pr          PR number
  files       png/jpg/gif/webm files

Options:
  --attach    also add them under the PR body's ## Screenshots section
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  nf shots 655 before.png after.png
  nf shots 655 shots/*.png --attach
```

### nanoflow ci

```text
Usage: nanoflow ci [options] [pr]

PR checks: status, --watch until done (no poll loops), the failing jobs' log tails, rerun failed

Arguments:
  pr               PR number (default: the current branch's PR)

Options:
  --watch          wait until no check is pending; exit 1 if any failed
  --timeout <min>  give up watching after this many minutes (default: "30")
  --failed-log     print the tail of each failed job's log
  --lines <n>      log lines per failed job (default: "60")
  --rerun-failed   re-run the failed jobs
  -h, --help       display help for command

Examples:
  nf ci
  nf ci 652 --watch --failed-log
  nf ci --rerun-failed
```

### nanoflow flow

```text
Usage: nanoflow flow [options]

one snapshot of every worktree (slot, services up, ticket, PR, CI) and the open tickets; the
nanoflow mod's provider

Options:
  --local     skip GitHub (fast: git + ports only)
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  nf flow
  nf flow --json
  nf flow --json --local
```

### nanoflow summary

```text
Usage: nanoflow summary [options]

the wrap-up footer for the current task, from live state: worktree, branch, PR, ticket, done, local
URL

Options:
  --what <text>      one line: what we did, product-level
  --next <items...>  next steps (one or more)
  --shipped <text>   only when something was released / deployed
  -h, --help         display help for command

Examples:
  nf summary --what "csv export for orders" --next "review + merge"
  nf summary --next "tear down" "watch errors" --json
```

### nanoflow init

```text
Usage: nanoflow init [options]

write a starter .claude/nanoflow.json from what the repo has (scripts, lockfile, .env files); --team
also offers the mod to teammates

Options:
  --board <owner/number>  your GitHub Project, e.g. acme/3
  --team                  add the nanoflow marketplace + plugin to .claude/settings.json
  --force                 overwrite an existing nanoflow.json
  -h, --help              display help for command

Examples:
  nanoflow init
  nf init --board acme/3 --team
```
